title: Lesson 16: Decision Trees, ID3, and Evaluation

slides.title: Decision trees: from examples to explainable rules

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Lesson sixteen turns fourteen historical loan applications into an explainable classifier. Each row supplies applicant attributes and a risk label; ID3 converts those labeled examples into a tree whose internal questions lead to high, moderate, or low risk leaves.

focuses.phrase: Lesson sixteen turns fourteen historical loan applications
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Lesson sixteen turns fourteen historical loan applications
kinetics.label: Ask the question that removes the most uncertainty

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Our anchor question is deceptively simple: which attribute should the tree ask about first? Guessing from appearance is not enough. We need a numerical rule that compares candidate questions by how much uncertainty each one removes.

focuses.phrase: Our anchor question is deceptively simple: which
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: We will move from data anatomy to tree traversal, recursive induction, entropy, information gain, rule extraction, and responsible evaluation. Think of the tree as a very disciplined twenty-questions player: every question must earn its place.

focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Induction is the mechanism. ID3 repeatedly chooses a test, partitions the current examples, closes pure partitions as leaves, and recursively treats each impure partition as a smaller learning problem.

slides.title: The target is risk; the evidence is past loan applications

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: The target variable is financial risk with three possible labels: high, moderate, and low. That is what the learner must predict. Credit history, debt, collateral, and income are predictors: evidence available before the decision.

focuses.phrase: The target variable is financial risk with
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: The target variable is financial risk with
kinetics.label: Predictors describe the case; the label names the target

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Do not mix target and predictor roles. If the answer column leaks into the inputs, the model can appear brilliant by peeking at the answer key. It is the machine-learning version of grading your own exam while holding the rubric.

focuses.phrase: Do not mix target and predictor roles.
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: A row is historical evidence, not a law of nature. The recorded label may reflect expert judgment, policy, measurement error, or past institutional behavior. ID3 learns patterns in those labels; it does not certify that the labels are fair or correct.

focuses.phrase: A row is historical evidence, not a
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Before modeling, ask who produced the labels, under which policy, for which population, and with what consequences. A technically accurate replica of a biased historical process can be an extremely efficient way to repeat history.

focuses.phrase: Before modeling, ask who produced the labels,
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Here is the mechanism-level distinction to keep: supervised learning estimates a mapping from predictors to a target using labeled examples. The tree does not discover risk as a physical substance hidden in the row. It discovers conditional regularities between the provided columns and the historical label. Change the labeling policy, feature definitions, or sampled population, and the learned concept can change even when the algorithm stays identical.

focuses.phrase: Here is the mechanism-level distinction to keep:
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

focuses.label: Frame

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Columns define the vocabulary available to the tree. Rows provide combinations of values and labels. ID3 can only ask questions expressible by these columns, so representation limits the hypotheses before the algorithm performs a single calculation.

focuses.phrase: Columns define the vocabulary available to the
focuses.label: Define

focuses.phrase: The set contains six high-risk, three moderate-risk,

segments.text: Visual inspection may suggest income is predictive, but eyesight is vulnerable to selective attention. We therefore inspect rows and columns, then replace intuition with a reproducible comparison of every candidate attribute.

A train-validation-test split changes the role of rows, not their format: training rows construct the tree, validation rows guide pruning or settings, and test rows estimate final generalization.

slides.title: ID3 learns a tree that describes class patterns

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: J. Ross Quinlan introduced ID3 in nineteen eighty-six. The historical detail matters because it separates a general model family, decision trees, from one specific induction procedure used to construct such a model.

focuses.phrase: J. Ross Quinlan introduced ID3 in nineteen
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: J. Ross Quinlan introduced ID3 in nineteen
kinetics.label: A tree is the representation; ID3 is the learner

segments.label: Define
segments.text: A decision tree represents a conditional concept as tests and outcomes. Internal nodes ask about attributes, branches correspond to observed values, and leaves store predicted classes. The finished tree can be executed and translated into human-readable rules.

focuses.phrase: A decision tree represents a conditional concept
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: ID3 is the learning mechanism. It uses labeled examples to choose tests greedily, partitions the data, and repeats. Saying the tree learned is shorthand; more precisely, ID3 induced a tree from evidence under a particular selection heuristic.

focuses.phrase: ID3 is the learning mechanism. It uses
focuses.label: Mechanism

slides.title: Internal nodes test attributes; leaves decide classes

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: The root is the first internal node and every example begins there. Its location gives it strategic importance: a useful root should organize the dataset into substantially cleaner subsets.

focuses.phrase: The root is the first internal node
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: The root is the first internal node
kinetics.label: Node asks; branch answers; leaf decides

segments.label: Define
segments.text: An internal node contains an attribute test such as forecast or income. It does not contain the final answer. Its job is to ask a question whose possible values determine which outgoing branch is followed.

focuses.phrase: An internal node contains an attribute test
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: A branch represents one answer value, such as sunny, overcast, or rain. A branch is neither a complete training record nor another probability formula; it is the labeled route created by the current test result.

focuses.phrase: A branch represents one answer value, such
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: A leaf terminates traversal and stores a class decision. The compact memory trick is: node asks, branch answers, leaf decides. If you confuse them, the tree becomes botanical modern art instead of an algorithm.

focuses.phrase: A leaf terminates traversal and stores a
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: Apply the distinction to the picnic example. Forecast is a node test, sunny is a branch value, humidity may be the next internal test, and yes or no is the leaf decision.

focuses.phrase: Apply the distinction to the picnic example.
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: A complete path can be read as nested conditionals. If forecast is sunny, then test humidity; if humidity is high, return no. That operational reading matters because tree depth approximates the number of questions asked for a particular case. Different leaves may have different depths, so prediction cost and explanation length can vary from one applicant to another.

focuses.phrase: A complete path can be read as
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

focuses.phrase: Choose option A, an attribute test. The

slides.title: A risk tree turns attribute values into a class

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: To classify an application, begin at the root. In the learned loan tree the first question is income because income produced the largest information gain during training.

focuses.phrase: To classify an application, begin at the
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: To classify an application, begin at the
kinetics.label: Classification follows one path, not every column

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Evaluate only the current node's attribute. If income is between zero and fifteen thousand dollars, the path immediately reaches high risk. Credit, debt, and collateral are not consulted for that case.

focuses.phrase: Evaluate only the current node's attribute. If
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Otherwise follow the branch matching the observed value and evaluate the next node. Middle income may require credit history and, for unknown credit, debt. High income may require credit history but not debt.

focuses.phrase: Otherwise follow the branch matching the observed
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Stop at the first leaf and return its class. Classification is therefore a conditional path, not a vote over every predictor. Unvisited attributes have no influence on that particular prediction.

focuses.phrase: Stop at the first leaf and return
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: Trace record two: income is fifteen to thirty-five thousand, credit is unknown, and debt is high, so the path terminates at high risk. Collateral appears in the table but nowhere in the learned tree.

focuses.phrase: Trace record two: income is fifteen to
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Consider an implementation detail. At a categorical node, the system must map the observed value to exactly one outgoing edge. An unseen value needs an explicit policy: use a default branch, the local majority class, probabilistic routing, or declare uncertainty. A classroom diagram often omits this engineering seam, but deployed software cannot solve it with a thoughtful shrug.

focuses.phrase: Consider an implementation detail. At a categorical
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: This interactive trace exposes the mechanism directly. The initial applicant has middle income, unknown credit, and high debt. The tree asks all three relevant questions before returning high risk.

focuses.phrase: This interactive trace exposes the mechanism directly.
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: This interactive trace exposes the mechanism directly.
kinetics.label: Changing one value can reroute the whole explanation

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Change income to the low band. The tree now stops immediately at high risk. Credit and debt remain visible input values, yet they are causally irrelevant to this traversal because the path never reaches those tests.

focuses.phrase: Change income to the low band. The
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Change income to the high band and credit to good. The route becomes income greater than thirty-five thousand, then good credit, then low risk. Debt is skipped, demonstrating instance-specific explanations.

focuses.phrase: Change income to the high band and
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Return to middle income, unknown credit, and switch debt from high to low. The leaf changes from high to moderate. A useful explanation reports the exact path taken and the plausible neighboring change that would alter the result.

focuses.phrase: Return to middle income, unknown credit, and
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: This counterfactual exploration must be interpreted carefully. Changing income in the interface shows how the model output changes while holding other represented values fixed. It does not prove that changing a person's real income would causally change financial risk. The tree is an associational predictor learned from records, not a randomized economic experiment.

focuses.phrase: This counterfactual exploration must be interpreted carefully.
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: ID3 recursively turns impure partitions into subtrees

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Read ID3 as executable pseudocode. The procedure receives a set of labeled examples and a set of unused attributes, then returns either a class leaf or a decision subtree.

focuses.phrase: Read ID3 as executable pseudocode. The procedure
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Read ID3 as executable pseudocode. The procedure
kinetics.label: Base cases stop; the recursive case grows

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Base case A handles purity. If every current example has the same class, return that class as a leaf. Continuing to split would add structure without reducing uncertainty.

focuses.phrase: Base case A handles purity. If every
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Base case B handles exhausted attributes or an unusable partition. Return a default, commonly the local majority class. This is a policy choice needed when the representation cannot perfectly separate the labels.

focuses.phrase: Base case B handles exhausted attributes or
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: The recursive case selects the best attribute, creates one branch per value, partitions examples, and calls ID3 on each impure child with a reduced attribute set. The algorithm grows from the top downward.

focuses.phrase: The recursive case selects the best attribute,
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: The greedy line is the local attribute selection. ID3 commits to the highest-gain test now and does not backtrack later if a different root would have produced a better global tree.

focuses.phrase: The greedy line is the local attribute
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Track the recursive arguments precisely. Each call receives a subset of examples and usually removes the selected attribute from future consideration along that branch. If a branch receives no examples, the algorithm needs a fallback from its parent context. If labels remain mixed after attributes are exhausted, a majority or probabilistic leaf records unresolved uncertainty rather than inventing a new predictor.

focuses.phrase: Track the recursive arguments precisely. Each call
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: Select, partition, test purity, then recurse

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Stage one compares candidate attributes using the current subset and chooses the test with maximum information gain. At the root, that comparison uses all fourteen records.

focuses.phrase: Stage one compares candidate attributes using the
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Stage one compares candidate attributes using the
kinetics.label: Every child becomes a smaller learning problem

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Stage two creates one branch for each observed value and sends every example down exactly one branch. Partitioning conserves the records while changing which examples are considered together.

focuses.phrase: Stage two creates one branch for each
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Stage three checks each child for purity. A child containing only high-risk labels becomes a high-risk leaf because its entropy is zero and no further question is required.

focuses.phrase: Stage three checks each child for purity.
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Stage four recurses on every impure child using its local rows and remaining attributes. Different branches can choose different next tests because their class distributions differ.

focuses.phrase: Stage four recurses on every impure child
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: This is divide and conquer with a statistical compass: split the big problem, close the easy pieces, and repeat on the messy pieces until a stopping condition fires.

focuses.phrase: This is divide and conquer with a
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: The invariant across stages is that each training example reaches exactly one current frontier node. Partitioning reorganizes the same evidence; it does not duplicate favorable rows or discard inconvenient ones. At every frontier, ask two questions in order: is the subset already pure, and if not, which remaining test most reduces its entropy? That pair drives the entire recursive construction.

focuses.phrase: The invariant across stages is that each
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: If several trees fit the data, which one should we prefer?

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Many different trees can classify all training rows correctly. A large tree may memorize rare combinations, label noise, or accidental details rather than capturing a pattern that survives beyond the sample.

focuses.phrase: Many different trees can classify all training
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Many different trees can classify all training
kinetics.label: Perfect training fit does not guarantee generalization

segments.label: Define
segments.text: A smaller tree has lower description cost and is easier to inspect. Simplicity acts as an inductive preference: among similarly supported hypotheses, prefer one that explains more with fewer tests.

focuses.phrase: A smaller tree has lower description cost
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: But shortest is not automatically best, accurate, or fair. Validate on unseen data. Simplicity is a useful seat belt, not a magical force field against every modeling mistake.

focuses.phrase: But shortest is not automatically best, accurate,
focuses.label: Mechanism

slides.title: A useful pattern compresses the data it explains

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Minimum message length formalizes a compression intuition. Choose the hypothesis H sub i minimizing the length needed to describe the hypothesis plus the length needed to describe the data given that hypothesis.

focuses.phrase: Minimum message length formalizes a compression intuition.
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Minimum message length formalizes a compression intuition.
kinetics.label: Good compression balances model and exceptions

segments.label: Define
segments.text: The first term is model cost. A deep tree with many tests, branches, and exceptional leaves requires more bits to specify than a compact tree. Complexity spends part of our explanatory budget.

focuses.phrase: The first term is model cost. A
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The second term is residual cost. A tiny model that explains almost nothing leaves a long list of errors or exceptions. Saying everything is complicated is short, but it does not compress the observations.

focuses.phrase: The second term is residual cost. A
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: The winner balances both terms. Think of packing for a trip: a suitcase the size of a building is wasteful, but one sock and heroic optimism will create expensive residual problems.

focuses.phrase: The winner balances both terms. Think of
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: The source's even-number example contains fifty integers from two through one hundred inclusive, not forty-nine. The correction strengthens the lesson: the phrase all even integers from two to one hundred is far shorter than listing all fifty.

focuses.phrase: The source's even-number example contains fifty integers
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: MML also reveals why memorization can look deceptively compact on tiny data. A rule listing fourteen row identifiers may classify the training set perfectly, but its hypothesis description grows with the dataset and says little about new rows. A genuinely reusable pattern pays a modest fixed model cost, then describes many observations cheaply. Compression becomes evidence of structure only when the coding scheme and evaluation protocol are honestly specified.

focuses.phrase: MML also reveals why memorization can look
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: Entropy measures uncertainty in a class distribution

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Information content for a class c is negative log base two of its probability. A rare event has high information because observing it is surprising; a certain event has zero information because it tells us nothing new.

focuses.phrase: Information content for a class c is
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Information content for a class c is
kinetics.label: Entropy asks how surprising the next label is

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Entropy H of S is the probability-weighted average information across classes: negative sum over p of c times log base two p of c. The unit is bits because the logarithm uses base two.

focuses.phrase: Entropy H of S is the probability-weighted
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Use the convention zero log zero equals zero by continuity. A class absent from the subset contributes nothing, rather than causing the calculation to explode into mathematical confetti.

focuses.phrase: Use the convention zero log zero equals
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: A pure set has entropy zero because the next label is certain. For two classes, a fifty-fifty set has entropy one bit, the maximum binary uncertainty. With three balanced classes the maximum is log base two of three, about one point five eight five bits.

focuses.phrase: A pure set has entropy zero because
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Example
segments.text: Entropy describes the label distribution inside a set, not the visual complexity of a drawn tree. It is the messiness of the answer pile before we ask another question.

focuses.phrase: Entropy describes the label distribution inside a
focuses.label: Example

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Derive the binary maximum explicitly. Let p be the positive fraction, so H of p equals negative p log two p minus one minus p log two of one minus p. The function is symmetric around one half and its derivative is zero there. The second derivative is negative, confirming a maximum. You do not need calculus to run ID3, but the shape explains the slider rather than asking students to worship it.

focuses.phrase: Derive the binary maximum explicitly. Let p
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: Purity lowers entropy; a 50/50 split maximizes it

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: The slider controls a binary set of ten examples. With five positives and five negatives, each probability is one half, so entropy equals negative two times one half log base two one half, which is exactly one bit.

focuses.phrase: The slider controls a binary set of
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: The slider controls a binary set of
kinetics.label: Balanced classes are maximally uncertain

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Move to ten positives and zero negatives. The positive term becomes one times log two of one, which is zero, and the absent class contributes zero. The set is pure and entropy falls to zero.

focuses.phrase: Move to ten positives and zero negatives.
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Move to eight positives and two negatives. Entropy is about zero point seven two two bits. The labels are mixed, but less uncertain than the fifty-fifty case because one class is substantially more likely.

focuses.phrase: Move to eight positives and two negatives.
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret

The rules may overlap after later simplification, so an implementation then needs a conflict policy. In the original unsimplified tree, mutually exclusive branch tests ensure one case follows one path and reaches one conclusion.

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Treat high risk as the positive class. True positives are correctly flagged high-risk cases; false negatives are truly high risk but missed. False positives are flagged but not truly high risk; true negatives are correctly unflagged.

segments.text: Precision equals true positives divided by all predicted positives. It asks: among the applications we flagged, what fraction were actually positive? High precision limits false alarms.

focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Recall equals true positives divided by all actual positives. It asks: among all truly high-risk cases, what fraction did we find? High recall limits misses.

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It becomes high only when both are reasonably high, but it still hides true negatives and does not encode the real-world cost of each error.
